sentences.text: It is contended on behalf of the accused-petitioner that no case for the alleged offences is made out against him and his [2024:RJ-JD:2280] (2 of 3) [CRLMB-298/2024] incarceration is not warranted as the victim is a consenting party.
There are no factors at play in the case at hand that may work against grant of bail to the accused-petitioner and he has been made an accused based on conjectures and surmises.

3. Contrary to the submissions of learned counsel for the petitioner, learned Public Prosecutor opposes the bail application and submits that the present case is not fit for enlargement of accused on bail.
4. Have considered the submissions made by both the parties and have perused the material available on the record as well as the case dairy.

After going through the statement of the victim it is revealing that victim Mst.'M' is a 19 years old girl; she has made allegation against the petitioner of taking away her forcibly into the Court and to solemnize marriage with her; the essence of her statement recorded under Section 164 Cr.P.C. before the Magistrate on 15.03.2021 that she was forced to marry with the petitioner.
On the contrary, the document submitted along with the bail application revealing that the petitioner and the victim moved an application for solemnizing their marriage.
The affidavit duly executed and notorised on which her photograph is affixed revealing that she married with the petitioner at her own free will and volition.

The coloured photographs annexed with the bail application reflecting that the victim was garlanding the petitioner and they were offering religious rituals around the 'Altar'; they can be seen in a jovial and pleasant mood.

Ration card of the petitioner has been placed on record for perusal of the Court in which the name of his wife has been mentioned as 'Manju', who is [2024:RJ-JD:2280] (3 of 3) [CRLMB-298/2024] the victim of this case.
The passbook issued by the Punjab National Bank has also been submitted before the Court to show marital relations between the petitioner and the victim.
5. In this view of the matter looking to the fact that keeping the petitioner behind the bars would not be justifiable as there is high probability that the trial may take long time to conclude.
Thus, without commenting on the merits of the case, it is deemed suitable to grant the benefit of bail to the petitioner in the present matter.
6. At a pre-conviction stage; bail is a rule and denial from the same should be an exception.
The purpose behind keeping an accused behind the bars during trial would be to secure his presence on the day of conviction and that he may receive the sentence as would be awarded to him.

Otherwise,
it is the rule of Crimnal Jurisprudence that he shall be presumed innocent until the guilt is proved.

7. Accordingly, the instant bail application under Section 439 Cr.P.C. is allowed and it is ordered that the accused-petitioner as named in the cause title shall be enlarged on bail provided he furnishes a personal bond in the sum of Rs.50,000/- with two sureties of Rs.25,000/- each to the satisfaction of the learned trial Judge for his appearance before the court concerned on all the dates of hearing as and when called upon to do so.

FARJAND ALI),J 812-Mamta/-
